guide.summary: Forgejo documents an authorization-code OAuth2 provider with per-user consent, and its API accepts OAuth access tokens as Bearer tokens. OAuth2 scopes are not implemented, so the token is not scope-limited and can perform any action on behalf of the user. Read-only use is a property of the app's own behavior, not of the token. The repository search endpoint documents page and limit pagination and a private parameter that defaults to true, but no separate grant identifier is documented for it. Customer instance URLs must be supplied per instance. Registration, consent and the token exchange are setup steps that remain untested.

findings.title: Authorization-code OAuth2 with per-user consent is documented
findings.detail: Forgejo acts as an OAuth2 provider for third-party apps with the user's consent, using the Authorization Code grant with PKCE; confidential and public client types are supported. Registration is done in user settings and the token is sent as a Bearer header.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer connects their own account on their own instance

findings.title: OAuth2 scopes are not implemented; tokens act with full user rights
findings.detail: OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented and OAuth2 tokens can execute any action on behalf of the user. Third-party applications obtaining a token for a user via an OAuth2 application have administrative rights. Read-only use is therefore a property of the app's own behavior, not of the token.

evidence.quote: OpenID Connect (OIDC) To use the Authorization Code Grant as a third-party application, it is required to register a new application via the “Settings” ( /user/settings/applications ) section. To test

It is possible for any user to manually register a new OAuth2 application on the /user/settings/applications page for the purpose of using Git credential helpers different from the pre-registered ones.

Visit https://codeberg.org/user/settings/applications and create a new OAuth2 application. There needs to be only one redirect URI, composed with the arbitrary name that was chosen above: https://forgejo.example.com/user/oauth2/Codeberg/callback .

findings.title: Repository search pagination and private-repository default are documented without a grant identifier
findings.detail: GET /api/v1/repos/search documents page and limit parameters for pagination and a private parameter that includes private repositories the user has access to, defaulting to true. No separate OAuth grant identifier is documented for this endpoint, so no permission finding is created.
